messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected at 06:20 UTC — elevated 95th-token latency on continuous-batcher pool (us-west-2). Multiple nodes showing persistent GPU paging and occasional container restarts. Auto-alerting on-call.
Maya: seeing it, joining. summary pls and impact?
Tony: brief: around 06:18 we saw batch size growth on a subset of requests (long sequences) -> KV prefetch kept growing, OOMs started at 06:19. CUDA driver log shows repeated page faults and 'out of memory' on process pid 4211. A few containers restarted by kube.
Tony: logs snippet:
```
[06:19:12] runtime: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN: page fault, attempting migration
[06:19:18] batcher: accum_size=32768 prefetch_kv_nodes=184K
[06:19:20] oom: failed alloc 1.2G, killing process 4211
```
Sarah: customers affected? any 5xx spikes or error budgets? :eyes:
Maya: dashboards — small set of customers (3 mid-market tenants) hit 5xxs and timeouts; broad tail latency increased service-wide. No global outage but SLO windows at risk. Support already flagged 2 P1s.
Eli: can we isolate which model / route? maybe a recently rolled model/commit triggered prefetch behavior.
Tony: root route is rtx-2-big mixed-quant model; there was a deployment at 05:45 that adjusted kv-prefetch from 1s -> 3s (intended to reduce cold misses). That likely increased kvcache churn for long-context traffic.
Maya: immediate mitigation options: 1) revert kv-prefetch change; 2) throttle prefetch per-request; 3) route to fallback smaller model; 4) evacuate pods on nodes with repeated GPU pagefaults.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2931abce started at 05:45:12 — change: kv_prefetch_window=3s
Tony: +1 revert. I can roll back the config for the pool (canary first) and throttle prefetch param to 0.5s.
Eli: while Tony reverts, I'll start controlled drain of the 3 most noisy nodes and cordon them. kube events show node-flip and GPU driver errors on ip-10-0-4-101, ip-10-0-4-107, ip-10-0-4-109.
Maya: assign handoff: I'm primary until 06:35 then Eli will take over for mitigation steps. @Eli you good to take over if Tony needs help with rollback?
Eli: yep. will take 06:35-07:00. starting drain now.
Maya: Tony, any risk that draining will cause additional scheduling and amplify batch growth elsewhere?
Tony: risk exists — draining will move pods, increasing scheduling pressure. We'll perform slow drain with pod eviction delay and temporarily scale up a few spare GPU nodes to absorb traffic.
Maya: ok create temporary nodepool 3 nodes (g4dn equivalent) and scale pool by +3, set autoscaler min cap. Sarah, can you ping infra to approve quick quota bump?
Sarah: pinged infra and finance channel — approving emergency hot nodes, ETA ~4m. :thumbsup:
Tony: rolling back kv_prefetch change in canary now. command:
```
opsctl deploy rollback --pool continuous-batcher-usw2 --revision 2931abce --canary 10%
```
Tony: canary shows initial success — no OOMs in canary pods for 2m, latency stable.
incident-bot: Alert suppression engaged for rolling rollback; keeping high-fidelity logs for 10m.
Maya: start routing rules: divert 20% traffic for heavy-context routes to cpu-fallback models to reduce GPU pressure.
Tony: routing change applied. Monitoring for error increases.
Eli: drain in progress. observed kube evict events, redis patching of KV mappings triggered, prefetch counters for cordoned nodes stopped spiking.
Maya: update on customer impact: affected tenants still see elevated p95 but 5xxs dropping. support holding on outward comms until we confirm stability.
Tony: got a weird secondary issue: one node's CUDA driver crashed during drain (ip-10-0-4-107). Container restarted and rejoined, but kernel logs show 'NVIDIA: GPU page fault: persistent' — I've flagged to eng-runtime to check driver stability. opening infra ticket.
Sarah: support update posted: "We are investigating elevated latency and intermittent errors; mitigation underway. ETA 30-60m." (copied to customers).
Maya: after 10m checks, rollback fully applied. no further OOMs observed in rolling logs, tail latency improving. but prefetch growth back-pressure still needs addressing long term.
Eli: created short-term guard: per-request prefetch budget of 128MB and a hard cap on KV nodes per-request. also added a watchdog that kills batches exceeding 1M tokens aggregated across window.
Tony: pushing post-incident followups: 1) revert or make kv-prefetch adaptive based on node memory; 2) add soft limits to continuous-batcher accumulator; 3) better eviction policy so KV prefetch doesn't grow unbounded for long seqs; 4) improve driver monitoring to detect early paging patterns.
Maya: agree. assign action items: Tony -> rollback verification and canary test plan, Eli -> node driver triage & reproduce paging locally, Sarah -> customer comms & incident timeline, Maya -> postmortem and severity classification.
Eli: quick note — we saw one container crash that left orphaned shared memory regions that made subsequent containers slower; cleaned up with:
```
sudo ipcrm -M 0x12345678
```
Tony: marking incident as 'mitigated' at 06:33 UTC — we'll keep watch for 60m, if no regressions we move to resolved but with a required postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident mitigated by rollback and node draining. Status: MONITORING. Pager duties transferred to Eli at 06:35 UTC.
Maya: handing off to Eli now. I'll be available if anything escalates. Good job team, let's avoid repeating the fix being auto-promoted.
Eli: taking over watch. will update at 06:50 with stability check. :eyes:
Maya: (reaction) :heart:
